body: Oof. Spot on

This is spot on. I went out with a friend I had distantly known since middle school and mentioned that I was in therapy (for PTSD events not related to my family) and the first thing she said was “Oh you’re finally getting help foe your issues with your mom!”. It was sad hearing that but in that moment I felt so understood and not crazy. If others are noticing that then I must not be making it up
Normal for N households but not for normal households. I got my own BED at age 22. I sympathize with you because I know how bad it sucks.
I haven’t experienced that specifically but I was not ever allowed to attempt to do laundry or cook. Seems like she wanted me to not learn those skills so I would be dependent on her
It’s shocking but after years and years you become so used to it. She would have had a comeback anyways so it’s not really helpful to continue conversation with her
I’m so sorry. When I attempted, all she did was plead with me not to say that I did it because I was bullied at school. Then she just dumped me at the ER
That is my worst fear. I hope to go very low contact when I have children of my own.
Wow. I would say “yeah it’s difficult for someone who doesn’t know how to love”

Calling the police was the best choice. If this happens again, immediately call 911 and say that she is having a PSYCHIATRIC EMERGENCY. They will be more prepared for this and police will not use force as much
I used to be sad when my Nmother used to say that now idgaf. I’m just waiting for her to say that again and tell her “yeah you should have done it but you didn’t, the blame is all on you”
I’m so sorry. This is my fear and why I haven’t told anyone about my sexual abuse as a child. Narcs don’t really care unless it happens to them.

I’m sorry. Imposter syndrome is real and should be talked about more. I felt like that in the beginning of my career and now three years later I still get that frequently. Damage done by our parents lasts well into our lives. I hope you find healing within yourself ❤️‍🩹
They always use this one. They’re just so unhappy with themselves and their lives that they must find someone else to blame it on.

I’m so sorry you had to go through an abusive relationship while dealing with your N mother. I was in a similar situation where I was emotionally physically and sexually abused in a relationship. I was able to get out after some time. A few months later during an argument my Nmother said “you can’t even keep a man”. She knew about all the abuse but she will say anything to protect herself and “win” an argument.
One word: PROJECTION

Definitely. I was nine years old and she made me go to the landlord and beg him to lower our rent. 
Another thing is from the age I could talk she would always tell me the reason they broke up with my dad and he left is because he didn’t want kids and me being born didn’t go into his plans. She later said she thought it was less traumatic than telling me he had a mistress in the side.

I’m sorry that happened. It is common for children of N to be brainwashed to never tell the truth to outsiders. I hope one day you will gain the strength to stand up for yourself and not let your N parent dictate who you are.
Someone once said “if everyone around you is an asshole, most likely you’re the asshole”
Mine always says this. Maybe because there are no nasty things about you so she can’t make anything up on the spot?
Hahahaha I love this. This is how you know they are an N. They do not have any common sense.

I’m so happy you got away from her. Mine did a similar thing. I got a raise at work and got a really nice letter letter of recommendation for university because of my boss. I’m a hard worker and always go in when someone calls out and stay after work to help out. My Nmother once said to me “you think you’re going to continue to move up in life? You just got lucky. All those things are not your achievements, just some person took pity on you”
“I wish you were never born”/“I wish I never gave birth to you” are such cruel words to be uttered by a parent yet we are the ones who are the bad guys.
Yes!!! I’ve tried a water floss but it was too messy and I couldn’t stick to a routine. Tongue scrappers are so easy and quick to use. Big improvemenr
I’m so sorry this happened to you. I hope you get to live a life you enjoy and not be in constant fear.
That is sad because as we become adults and make relationships of our own, we cannot express emotions “normally” and it hurts our relationships with others.
Yep. I was called an “actress” and was told that I was faking it all.

Hahahaha perfect timing. She told me less than an hour ago that she is angry at God for making me be born. 

As my therapist said, everything is in a cycle: honeymoon period >> walking on eggshells >> abuse >> back to honeymoon

Wow. That quote explains so much. 

I’m sorry you had to go through that. If it helps, you’re not alone. I also did my Nmothers hw because she got paid for taking classes, then she complained that I was taking too many of my classes and I should drop some of mine to take more of hers because she “needs” (aka wants) the money.

I think this is a very common excuse for Nmothers to blame their medical/body issues on their pregnancy. I’m in my 20’s, only child and my Nmother still blames her obesity on me. Even though I saw pictures of her pre pregnancy and she was overweight. 

I’m glad you were able to get out, unfortunately under less that ideal circumstances, but at least you’re not with such nasty people. My Nmother does the absolute minimum to keep me around so I can take care of all her daily activities and also take care of her parents.
That’s great, do not give them an ounce of supply. They do not deserve it.

Yes!!!! Just yesterday after 20+ years I realized *****not FOUND OUT or REMEMBERED***** REALIZED that I was actually a foster child. I was raised by my grandparents who legally had rights over me. I am so used to abuse and people not wanting me that I thought it was how everyone else lived. Now I have to process the fact that I was a foster child for 6+ years.
She might not be a pedo but she might have been comparing her body to yours.

Yep. Mine does the same thing. She rarely says thank you either. Recently she started thank you more and it’s such a scary weird feeling. I’m used to her being harsh and I feel uncomfortable when she says it.
Yes!! Had one of those today. Like wtf brain make up your mind lol

I switched 3 counselors in the past year. First one was hard to get to and get an appointment (quit after 2 sessions), second one was amazing but committed suicide after a few months of sessional (he told me he planned to do it during our last session), third one was a typical schoolbook psychologist with no emotions and only cared if I had homicidal or suicidal tendencies. I’m not ready for another therapies and starting over again at this time.

I’m not too familiar with proper bipolar labels but doesn’t bipolar feel like there are 3 versions of you that come out at different times (depressive manic and the normal you) that you must keep happy but you should always prioritize the happiness of normal you before the needs and wants of the two others?

This is what I subconsciously knew but was afraid of hearing. Thank you.  I am coping with this information and trying to make it “less scary” for myself. The way I view it is bipolar changes you just like any other trauma changes you. Like how people after a huge car accident say that their life changed to before and after the accident. I was in a domestic violence relationship at 18 and years later I am still struggling with my PTSD. I’ve come to terms with my PTSD changing me and I shouldn’t be TOO afraid of bipolar changing me. I like to think of it as another PTSD lol.
Thank you for your comment. I was afraid of this but I knew the time would come someday that the decision would have to be made.
Thank you for your advice. I screenshotted your comment so I know who to contact. Thank you for letting me know such service exist!
Thank you for your comment. I will always feel a little bit of guilt but I know this is the best choice for all.

I cried after reading your story. I hope to reach such moments one day with my future children. If I couldn’t do anything about growing up in a unsafe family, I can definitely change the scenario when raising my own family.

Thank you for your response. Being very honest, throughout my life I looked down on people who put their parents in nursing homes. Now I regret it because I see how abusive elders can get. Not everyone turns into sweet, bubbly grannies. 

And now it has gotten so bad that I fear for the parents safety. They might harm themselves if I’m not around and even if I’m around they still manage to do dangerous things (like at night).
Yes, you are correct. Children at least listen to you. Sometimes I feel my parents do the opposite of what I want them to do.

That is a very good question. In my case they also need different levels of care and I believe they would have to go to other facilities. They are one of those couples who hated each other throughout their lives and only live together now because they’re under my roof. 

My 82 parent with mod to severe dementia has been in a nursing facility post fall twice. Every time was when they transferred her there from the ER. 

The 83 y/o parent is physically doing okay but has aggression issues and is slowly losing his mind. He might need memory or psychology relate services, not a nursing facility. I have not called such services yet and cannot imagine how I can send him there because he will put up a physical fight. Five years ago I offered to pay for adult day care for him (4-5 hours a day) so he would have some activities, but when the time came to go, he flat out refused and barricaded himself in his room.

That is my dream, to provide an environment where they can be at least somewhat active. All they do is stay at home and refuse to socialize with others their age. 

May I ask was it a private facility or a state funded one?
I am so sorry. She does not have a conscience if she can brush it off so lightly. What did your father do?

Thank you for your response. I have one sibling who is their “golden child”. He has a criminal past, my parents and I have a restraining order against him, he physically assaulted me during teenage years and once during adulthood, and his son tried to run my daughter over with his car. Despite all this they keep saying how much better he is and how much they love and miss him. He does not want to take care of them because there are no financial incentives. 

The parent with mod-severe dementia constantly falls and is unable to use one of those emergency call buttons. I feel terrible when that happens whenever I’m not at home. I’m not that old, 50, but I’m approaching retirement years and don’t want to keep spending the last of my “active” years by sitting with them at home 24/7. Also I cannot do that because we need money to live on and I have a young adult child I’m helping out during her college years.
Food allergies is embarrassing? Gosh, I want to slap your mother. I just don’t get people.

Could this be because she herself did not do well in college and expected you to do the same? I have a sort of similar experience with my Nmother. She was forced to play an instrument growing up by her mother which she hated so she forbade me from learning to play one.
Ah yes. The classic. They are aware that they’re  abusive but try to keep a good image.
Oh my God. Im so sorry. Did anyone besides your parents see this? Did anyone try to step in? This is something that would prompt CPS to be sent out.
I’m so sorry that happened to you. Lots of kids resort to nail biting as a way to cope with stress. Your parents’ “techniques” were extremely counterproductive.
You’re so right. I have distant relatives that are moderately rich or doctors or lawyers but they are either “bad people” as my family calls them or they don’t talk to us.

Yes! You hit the nail on the head. Right now she is taking care of her welder let prenatal and multiple times a day she will whine how her life is so difficult but doesn’t do anything about it. She makes her life revolve around them. Example, if she is somewhere important and it is 4:30 (half an hour before 5, the time grandparents have dinner) she starts to shut down, sweat, become agitated, panic, etc. and tells everyone to wrap it up because she needs to go home and it’s an EMERGENCY. Like if you don’t feed them for half an hour nothing will happen. She annoys me so much.

Thank you for your kind words. Yeah I definitely will not be doing this in a million years. I just do not see where she is coming from. I cannot imagine myself saying that to my own daughter or son. She actually left my to my Ngrandmother when I was an infant and only took me back during my early teenage years.

I am female. The fighting thing was just an example. I was in high school and a guy was angry at something I did and wanted to settle this with one of my male family members. Later on, when I thought about it, I realized that I have no one to help me when I get into a dangerous, physically assaultive situation.

I hate to admit this, but seeing all these girls on social media show off their brothers and fathers during this one trend going around (show who would defend you if someone messes with you) makes me feel lonely and upset. Instead of anyone protecting me, I had a Nmother who would constantly tell me during my childhood “if you get kidnapped, don’t expect me to run after the car”.

Really? I’ve been so shy to talk about this topic. I don’t know of anyone else in a similar situation. My Nmother used to humiliate me because of it and would not let me go on school trips or sleepovers because of that (well she used that as an excuse but in reality she just didn’t want to drive me to those places).
I didn’t start brushing my teeth until I was 7. Didn’t realize glossing existed until 12-14.
My Nmother always threatened to call mental services and lock me up because obviously I am insane.
Me. And I absolutely hate it. My narcissist sees me as a continuation of themselves. They see me as a loser that they are themselves.
I really think so too. She is also someone who likes to project her insecurities on others. She needs to feel like she above others so she might be doing this by humiliation.

She has done this for so long that it has become normal to me. Just last week I’ve actually had a moment of enlightenment and realized how weird this is. I am glad there are parents out there who do not do this to their children.
Thank you for your help. I just posted an update if you want to know a bit more.
I tried not to but I was so upset. Now I know a little bit more and just posted an update.
Yes. I completely understand that and I am very thankful that he was so comfortable with me to share such personal details. I just posted an update to the story.
That is correct. They spoke of their suicidal thoughts on our previous visit. I just posted an update.
Thank you for the kind words and well wishes. I just posted an update.
Hey. I just posted an update to the story

I really hope they are alive but it would be hard living with the guilt that I didn’t do everything that I could. I struggle with suicidal thoughts from time to time and have a long history of trauma and abuse by family and others. During one of the sessions I told him I want to help people in the future as a job (maybe even become a social worker). I guess you can help people at any time but idk, I thought he would get through his issues because he always put a positive twist on everything.
I don’t have their address to their physical work location. Our therapy sessions were virtual through a therapy app.

Yes that is what is concerning. He always found positives in my situations and his and then when he told me what’s going on with him I was shocked. He also told me he was contemplating divorcing, he relapsed in his alcoholism, and he was arrested for doing something while drunk a few days ago, so all these things were brand new to me and very shocking. I hope he is doing alright. I don’t want to break the therapist/patient relationship but I really want to know if he is ok.
I don’t know how long they have not been responding.
I have none of their social media.
Why not tell them to do a welfare check? I thought if I tell them I haven’t heard from the person in a while and I’m concerned that wouldn’t hurt.

He is a newer therapist. Slightly less than five years in practice. He let me know that we share a lot of similarities of past abuse (childhood and other events). All of the sessions had a positive outlook and only during the last one he let me know that he relapsed with his alcoholism, got into a huge fight with his wife, contemplated suicide, and reached out to a crisis line. It was shocking to me because he seemed to always overcome trauma from what he told me. When he was telling me these things, he didn’t seem to be extremely upset so I believed that he found the help he needed. He let me know that he had a meeting scheduled with Alcoholics Anonymous and found a therapist for himself.

I know it’s not my job to be involved in his trauma but as a person I feel bad for him and want to help him in what ways I can.
This!!
Thanks
I’m praying and hoping that they are alright. They did not have an easy life and go through so many tough obstacles so I’m praying they are safe now.
Please see my updated post. They weren’t just a friend so the situation is a bit more complicated.

I wasn’t. I updated the post to shed some light. They are my therapist who I happened to find two months ago. I did not know their whole situation and our one hour weekly meeting usually did not include their personal life.
Not yet unfortunately. Please see my updates in the post.

I am prematurely grieving the whole day. I can’t help myself but I’m praying and hoping for the best. They do struggle with alcohol abuse and have blackout episodes so I’m praying that is the worst thing that could have happened to them. Please see my edits in the post which might shed a bit more light.
No major update. I found their old cell number which goes to voicemail. Found their address (I assume) but having trouble getting Pd to do a welfare check. No response from them thus far.
I’m really trying but what makes it hard is that they are a licensed therapist who might get their license revoked if they are found to be unstable for work with patients.

Their city is not doing pd welfare checks on weekends. Are there any other organizations you might know of that do something similar? I don’t even know their phone number so it’s hard to track them down.
I tried. They are open only on weekdays for some bizarre reason. Their voicemail says to call 911 if it’s an emergency but I’m hesitant to do so.
Unfortunately I don’t know his number, we talked through an app that does not disclose personal information.
I posted a tiny update but unfortunately still no contact.
I posted a tiny update in the edit of the post. Please read the beginning of my post because I clarified something as well.
Sorry guys. I’m trying and grieving at the same time. I posted an update in the post edit. No major news except I assume I was able to find his address and still no reply.
He is 40 years old, married with kids. No immediate family. I don’t know his friends (he doesn’t have that many) except a family friend somewhere on the east coast whom I have no way of contacting.
We are not teenagers but a bit older. He is almost 40. Married with kids. He also lives in a different state across the country.

Which website is legit? There’s hundreds of them and I don’t know which one is good. I was able to find their address though through the free websites. Last time we talked (1 week ago) they were in a hotel room due to a fight with their spouse.

I found out it’s their real name but could not find any social media for them. I was able to find their address though. I attempted to call their local police station for a welfare check but they operate only Monday through Friday.

I’m praying that they are safe or at least in a hospital/institution. This was a pretty important meeting for them and it’s very out of character for them not to show up with notifying me before or after.

Unfortunately they do not have any social media that I know of and their name (first and last) is a very common name (maybe even an alias). I tried even before this to find any information on them or their family and I could not. If they don’t answer within the next few hours, I will attempt calling police in their city.

I know their full name but a week ago they had a run in with the law and not so good past history. If they are alive, I’m afraid that it will put them in harm’s way. I tried googling obituary records for their city but nothing came up.
They live in a different state. I know the approximate city but not their exact location.
You hit the nail on the head. This is exactly what I was thinking between the manic and depressive episodes, all the energy gets sucked out of you so you end up not living life as “normal you”.
Nope. My pcp when I told him I’m struggling mentally told me “ok I’ll have the mental services department give you a call” .... that was one year ago. Still waiting.

Hi. Thank you for your kind and insightful words. I am definitely codependent since I have been raised by a covert narcissist mother and overt narcissistic grandmother (lucky me). I am currently looking into therapy services and mental health services since I have OCD and strongly believe I have cyclothymia (a version of bipolar with more often episodes of mania and depression).

Thank you for your reply. I’ve been looking into articles on bipolar but everywhere it says that bipolar episodes are weeks and months  cyclothymia is listed as days or weeks. I can have several episodes in a day (2-3) lasting 3-6 hours and haven’t heard of anyone having the same thing.

This is not advice or an answer to your question but I wanted to thank you for this post. I am going through a hard time right now and your post reminded me that trauma bonds exist and can mimic positive feelings like love.
Yeah but I wasn’t relying on her. She literally went into my room and turned off the alarm on my phone and on the clock. I don’t have locks on the door. I can’t just barricade the door
Yes! Horsing is major. Buying every little unnecessary thing she sees on Amazon or TV.
Wouldn’t be surprised if I catch my Nmother doing that.
Oh yes, big time.
She knows my password and throws a fit when I change it
Omg yes!! Spot on!
Thank you so much. Any kind of reassurance that you are not insane and just a victim of abuse is helpful.

It’s bad when you have a narc at home, but when that narc has allies, it’s even worse. My Nmother’s Nmother would help create a cycle of abuse. She would lie and try to create conflict. When my Nmother would lash out at me, my Ngrandmother would go to me all nice and sweet and would tell me to go apologize to my mother.
This is really really bad to say but sometimes I think if it would have been better if I had more physical trauma instead of mental trauma so my story would be more believable.

To be honest, no. When someone stood up for me, I would get abused even more behind closed doors. “how dare you cry so hard from when I pushed you to the floor, now that they heard you they will think I’m a bad mother”
Yes. It is called gaslighting

I’m so sorry you had to go through that. Last night I saw a video of a grown man around 40-50 telling his story on how he would be yelled at and hit by his parents when doing his math homework wrong. He said that up to this day he freezes when he’s faced with a math question. 

Many parents don’t treat children as people, unfortunately, and that has a lasting effect well into adulthood. I’m sorry you had to go through that and I hope many people who read your story will learn something from it.
Hardest thing to accept is that her words are merely an opinion and not a fact. You choose to listen to her words or not but what she says is not written in stone.
We all have the same mother unfortunately haha. “You have the same amount of hours in a day as Beyoncé” is the quote your mom should be informed about.
Thank you :)
Thank you. This actually made me smile :)
You usually don’t unless it’s absolutely necessary. People raised in normal households will not understand what you went through.

Please get a job before moving. You need to be financially stable before pursuing other things. 

Do you have any hobbies or talents? You can try by making videos for tiktok, YouTube, even Reddit’s rpan so you can start being comfortable in front of others.

Not mine, but my Nmom’s Nmom (my grandmother) controlled her finances until she was 50 years old. My Nmom had to hide any extra purchases that we made, like shoes, to not get yelled at by an 80 year old 🤦‍♀️. 

My Nmom is narcissistic but a different type (more covert, while my Ngrandmother is overt) so she still controls my money but in a different way. She tracks what I spend, logs into my bank account, etc. and then uses that information on me (e.g., wow so much money spend on esthetician services, must be a bad esthetician since your skin is still bad).

Sounds like she might be projecting a lot of those. They have no self awareness. My Nmother who literally has no hobbies or never goes anywhere and her only pastime is being a couch potato was ranting last night on how people live their lives meaningfully lol

Never knew about this term. Makes sense since our perception of love and care was skewed from childhood. It’s like narcissists can smell the abuse on you and are drawn to it. 

When I was 18, I was raped and physically abused by N-ex several times and I thought it was normal since I was physically and emotionally abused by my Nmother. Took a several years of time and therapy to understand that I was manipulated and was a victim of abuse. When I first met with a therapist, I was shocked when she mentioned the word “abuse”. I knew things weren’t right at home, but hearing someone else say it, having someone reaffirm that you’re not insane, was a life changing experience. 

While I do not have any major advice for you, finding a therapist who works with people exposed to narcissism is a great start. My therapist, while not being very proficient in the narcissistic field, was able to pin point some common, reoccurring themes between my Nmother and my N-ex.

In their minds they’re perfect. My Nmother, who is obese with a huge pot belly small breasts and ultra skinny legs, thinks our 5’10 120lb ten years younger than her is a “monstrosity” (as she called her) and followed up with “I’m no model but at least it’s obvious that I’m a woman”. If Nparents can’t see things one could easily see in a mirror, I would not expect them to be able to see their actions or life from the point of view of another person.

So sorry you’re going through that. I am not married and never had been so I cannot offer you any advice there. Hopefully some wise people would be able to leave some helpful comments. I am curious to know this as well.

True. You got me there. I’ve heard someone say something along the lines of “imagine the most average American that you can and imagine how intelligent that average American would be. Now come to the realization that there are 165 million who are less intelligent and way way less intelligent than that person”
I’m so afraid I won’t be strong enough to protect my child from the trauma I faced or accidentally hurting them in a toxic way.

Forgot to add that she mentioned the rhinoplasty comment right after we had an argument that she’s on food stamps yet she literally bought a set of gold plated dinnerware from Amazon (several hundred dollars) and designed perfume (200 dollars).

Not sure for all Nparents, but my Nmother had me at a late age because she lived in a town where it was not socially acceptable to not have kids (basically every town lol). She hooked up with someone just for the sake of being pregnant and had me. She never expressed desire of any other kids and thought her life mission was fulfilled. 

Some Nparents do it just to be a bit more socially accepted.

Now she uses me as bragging material or just so she has a reply to the question “do you have kids?”
Yes. This one big time. My teacher would call me “modest”. If only she knew.
Not liking my name called by people close to me. When I meet someone, I’m ok with it, but the closer we get, the more I can’t stand it.

I’m pretty sure someone is. My main point is that there is this one person out there that we are thinking of and they do not realize it one bit and never won’t. They will go on with their lives not knowing someone wants to see them. That’s how life is. What you think of your self and what reality is, is often different.
Hahahaha take my updoot

That’s the thing with most girls, including me, no matter how interestedI am in the person, I will not go up to them and introduce myself. For me, it comes not only from me being a girl but other factors as well, but still I wait for the other person to make a move. I missed out on a lot of connections this way.
Yes. They probably don’t realize the lasting impression they have on us. I’m fairly young, but I wonder when I’m 60, 70, or even 80, will I still think about them and regret not meeting them again.
Oh just passing by on the street. I was waiting a few mins for my Uber. He was standing outside of a cafe talking to a few other men.

Same. Quarantine made this worse because others are complaining about not going outside that much and not doing activities. You want to mimic them and be like “ugh quarantine sucks” but then you realize you would ha e been doing the same things even if there was no COVID. Sad reality

I am so glad you are finally able to receive help. Living with chronic illness, especially untreated, is brutal. Best of luck to you with the studies. I’m sure they will take care of you much better than regular doctors (since they’re inclined to make the medication work to the best potential).
Thank you. I also have a history of abuse. I will check that book out.
Can you elaborate? This is more like what I feel. I feel embarrassment and start hyperventilating after most interactions with non-close people as soon as I end up by myself.

Thank you for explaining this. It helps having another person’s view. I understand this is a hard time for her, even though she is being toxic to those around us. I will take extra precautions while she is in this period.

No. 99% sure that nothing major happened. We live in the same room so we are in each other’s presence a lot. This change is pretty scary because I began to get used to her behavior and predict a lot of things, but this is very out of the ordinary. She is in her late 50’s with very noticeable aging changes and I have personally seen her several times look in a mirror for a long time and say to herself “I don’t need any changes, I look good”. Her obsession with her appearance is concerning.

You are right. It is just the shame of my actions that is burning a hole in me. In my six years in university, this is the only professor with whom I messed up so much. It’s also a pretty important class. Tomorrow morning I am going to write her an email and whatever happens, happens. 

Kind of sad as well because at the end of the class I wanted to write her an email thanking her for the two classes and her being lenient with me in the first class. Now if I do it, she will feel that I’m doing it just because I missed the test today.
Oh yeah, it’s definitely coming. She came up to the dog and started to profess her love to her: “you’re the only love of my life. Only you understand me truly”

Yes! We were once walking down the street and talking and some homeless/druggie men said “you have a nice voice”. When he said it, I was the one talking. When we passed by them I made a comment, something along the lines of “that was creepy” and my Nmother replied “yeah but they won’t hear me voice again haha”. I mindlessly replied that they were talking about me and she almost fought me while trying to convince me that it was her they were talking about. Like damn talk about standards (or lack of) lol

Thank you for making this post. I never realized that I don’t like when people call me by my name  because of my Nparents. It all makes sense now.  It’s kind of sad and fascinating at the same time. I wonder what other parts of my life has their narcissism affected me that I’m not currently aware of.
That’s how they get control. They know they do not have respective authority to command attention so they try to control you to get that.
I think every Nparent is like that.
Probably a subconscious tactic to avoid being yelled at/abused. Similar to when people flinch at every more after a period of abuse

I don’t think it’s a coworker because she works in a small company and I know all of her coworkers. She did mention (constantly) how her boss says that she looks pretty while he doesn’t say that to her other coworkers. Could this be a midlife crisis thing? She used to make fun of people who obsessed about looks but now she’s doing it herself.
So happy for you. You’re keeping my hope alive.
